payload.approximation_regime: finite one-particle basis (STO-3G, 6-31G); the paper states neither approaches the complete-basis-set limit

assumptions.statement: Jordan-Wigner encoding fixed; results not shown to be invariant under other fermion-to-qubit encodings
exact diagonalization within the chosen basis, so no method error beyond basis truncation

payload.error_bound: none reported; no error bars, convergence study, or basis extrapolation
limitations: Nonstabilizerness here is a property of an encoding, not of the molecule; the paper says so explicitly and declines physical conclusions.
Peak position, dissociation-limit magic and the ordering between two fixed geometries are all shown to be basis-set sensitive.
No data, code, geometries, or numerical tolerances are provided, so none of the curves is reproducible from the paper alone.

object_mapping.source_value: $\mathcal{W}_\beta(\psi(R))$, stabilizer work of the qubit-encoded ground state
object_mapping.target_value: nonstabilizerness of the molecular electronic ground state at bond length $R$

object_mapping.source_value: Pauli spectrum of the Jordan-Wigner-encoded statevector
object_mapping.target_value: a basis- and encoding-dependent representation of the molecular state, not an intrinsic molecular property

object_mapping.source_value: finite minimal or split-valence basis, full CI within that basis
object_mapping.target_value: the physical molecule at the complete-basis-set limit

observables: $\mathcal{W}_\beta(\psi(R))$ evaluated from the full Pauli spectrum of the statevector
payload.physical_system: molecular hydrogen along the H-H dissociation coordinate, mapped to 4 qubits (STO-3G) or 8 qubits (6-31G) by Jordan-Wigner

producer.model: claude-opus-5 (single interactive execution; no separate reviewer process)
